claim: A collection member whose directory repeats one large table makes `extractFont` allocate the sum of every repeat
The CFF and cmap checks are skipped for WOFF input, and the CFF check runs only for an `OTTO` signature
A WOFF's output buffer is sized from recorded table lengths, up to 1032× the file size, before any table is inflated

triage.scenario: a 2 MB WOFF whose compressed tables each record `origLength = 1032 × compLength`. The ratio check passes, and `new ArrayBuffer(size)` asks for ~2 GB before `inflateInto` can find that the streams decompress to far less. The allocation either fails (the face fails to load, which is fine) or succeeds and holds 2 GB through every `await` of the inflate loop in a tab. The header's `totalSfntSize` (offset 16) states the real size and is never compared, nor is the buffer grown as tables actually inflate.

claim: WOFF inflation is bounded only by each table's declared `origLength`, not by anything tied to the file
The CFF check skips every `CFF ` table whose major version byte is not 1, not only CFF2
Kerning adds up every `kern` lookup across all scripts, so a pair kerned in two scripts' lookups is applied twice
The cmap and CFF checks read a different table than opentype.js parses when a tag is listed twice or a table's length runs past the file

triage.scenario: `tableOf` takes the first record with a tag, and returns null when `offset + length` runs past the file. opentype.js reads tables at their offset, ignores the length, and keeps the last record for `CFF `/`CFF2` and parses every `cmap` record. So (a) a truncated or damaged file whose `CFF ` or `cmap` record states an overlong length skips `checkCff`/`checkCmap` entirely, and opentype.js then parses the table from its offset; (b) a font listing `cmap` or `CFF ` twice has only the first copy checked. Either way the hang and heap blow-up the checks were written to refuse reach opentype.js. The same mismatch decides `glyf`/`loca` presence: an overlong `glyf` record makes the code treat a TrueType font as CFF. These should refuse a duplicate tag or out-of-file table, or check exactly what opentype.js will read.

claim: GPOS reader's work budget never counts subtables, so a small GPOS can still hang or exhaust memory in pairSubtables

triage.scenario: The kern feature lists 65535 lookup indices (a 131 KB list). The LookupList has 65535 offsets, all pointing at one type-2 lookup whose subTableCount is 65535. `subtablesOf` is memoized by *index*, not by lookup offset, so every index walks and pushes all 65535 subtable offsets. That is ~4.3e9 reads and an array of ~4.3e9 numbers from a font of a few hundred KB, which is an OOM or hang during registration. After that, every `kernOf` call walks them all again. `workBudget` exists to stop exactly this case ("tables share one long list"), but `pairSubtables` never calls `spend`. It should charge `count` per lookup, or memoize by lookup offset so a shared lookup is walked once.
triage.cause: subtable walk outside the work budget

claim: A thunk or Blob source is read twice when DOM text asks for the face before the canvas does
WOFF table inflation has no bound until it finishes, so a small damaged or hostile table can exhaust memory
`parseFontStyle` and `styleQualifierCount` decide "is this word a weight or slant" differently
A GPOS `kern` feature with no readable pair lookups suppresses the legacy `kern` table
loadFontOutlines / fontEmbedding report the status of a registration that was replaced while it loaded
CFF2 outlines (font.tables.cff2) are reported as truetype by embeddingOf, which misroutes PDF and SVG font embedding

triage.scenario: a variable OpenType font with a `CFF2` table and no `glyf`. The parser accepts it (`checkCff` handles CFF2, and opentype.js reads it), but `outlines` is `'cff'` only when `t.cff` is set. If opentype.js stores a CFF2 Top DICT anywhere other than `tables.cff`, the embedding says `'truetype'`, so a PDF writer embeds it as a TrueType program with no `glyf` table and the glyphs come out blank. The check should be on the sfnt's own tables (`tableOf(sfnt, 'CFF ') ?? tableOf(sfnt, 'CFF2')`, as the parser already does). The `FaceEmbedding.outlines` doc ("a `CFF ` table and no `glyf`") is silent on CFF2. Not verified: opentype.js is not installed in this tree.
triage.cause: outline kind read from parser state rather than tables

claim: A DOM-only read of a Blob or thunk source keeps a copy of the bytes for the registration's whole life
GPOS reader's feature/LangSys walk is unbounded: a crafted ~0.5 MB font hangs or exhausts memory at load
gposPairKerning's memo grows with no bound
`embeddable` refuses fonts whose fsType sets Restricted alongside a less restrictive bit
A WOFF face loses every kerning pair behind a GPOS Extension lookup, while the same font as TTF/OTF keeps them
Local fonts quote their `local()` name with JSON.stringify, not the package's CSS string quoter
checkCff never reads the FDArray's Font DICTs, so a CID-keyed CFF with a damaged FD `Private` reaches opentype.js unchecked
`enableLocalFontOutlines` replaces outline registrations the app already made for the same variant
The PostScript name is answered in two places, and the two can disagree
A .ttc whose member offsets all name one huge directory makes membersOf reread it per member, quadratic work on a damaged file

triage.scenario: A ttcf header has numFonts = 250 000 (1 MB of member offsets), and every offset names the same directory with numTables = 65535 (1 MB of records). `membersOf` calls `memberName` for every member, and each call builds the full 65535-record array just to find `name`. That is ~1.6e10 record objects from a 2 MB file, a hang inside `sfntFromCollection` before any parser runs. The `.dfont` path refuses a resource named twice for this reason ("cannot copy more than the file"), but the ttcf path does not dedupe directory offsets, and does not bound records × members. It could memoize by `dirOffset`, or refuse two members sharing a directory.
triage.cause: no dedupe of member directory offsets

claim: checkCff does quadratic work when many FDArray Font DICTs share one Private DICT's Subrs INDEX, rereading it each time

triage.scenario: An FDArray INDEX holds 65535 small Font DICTs (~5 bytes each), each with a `Private` operator naming the same Private DICT, whose `Subrs` names one 65535-item INDEX (offSize 1 with zero-length items, ~64 KB). `readIndex` re-walks and re-allocates the 65535 items for every Font DICT: ~4.3e9 iterations from a CFF table of under 0.5 MB. The structural check meant to keep a damaged face from holding the thread becomes the hang. Checking each distinct `(at, size)` Private and each Subrs offset only once bounds it by the table size.
triage.cause: shared Private/Subrs re-read per Font DICT

claim: `advanceOf` lets a CFF charstring parse throw into layout, unguarded, while `glyphD` for the same glyph is caught
`.dfont` type and reference counts handle the stored-minus-one 0xffff two different ways

The per-face glyph memo has no bound
GPOS lookup indexes are not checked against LookupList's count, so a bad index reads another table's bytes as a lookup
`FaceEmbedding.embeddable`'s doc says bit 1 always forbids embedding, but the parser allows it for OS/2 v0–2 fonts
WOFF unpacking copies repeated and overlapping table records, which `.ttc` and `.dfont` refuse
GPOS ScriptList records sharing one Script table multiply LangSys iteration past the work budget

triage.scenario: a GPOS whose ScriptList holds 65,535 records all pointing at one Script table with 65,535 LangSys records (~800 KB of tables). `langSysesOf` memoizes the Script table, so `spend(langSysCount)` is charged once, but `scripts` gets one entry per record sharing the same `langSysAt`, and the loop at line 149 walks all 65,535 × 65,535 ≈ 4.3e9 entries doing a `langSysSeen.has` each. The budget (4 per byte, ~3.2M here) never trips, and the face's load hangs for minutes. Dedupe `scripts` by Script table offset, or spend per record walked.
triage.cause: memoized table shared by records, iteration not budgeted

claim: A warn-once key is the variant, not the registration, so a re-registered face that fails again warns nothing
A local variable font registers its default instance's outlines under every named instance's weight
An empty `postscriptName` counts as absent for `cssSrc` but as a name for the parser
An empty PostScript name selects the collection's first member and reports a match
Pairs kerned only under a language-specific LangSys get kerned in default text

triage.scenario: `lookupIndexSets` emits one set per LangSys: `latn` default, then each `latn` language system (e.g. `NLD `, `TRK `), then `DFLT`. `pairKerning` returns the first set that kerns the pair. A pair that `latn` default leaves unkerned but a language-specific LangSys kerns gets that language's adjustment in ordinary Latin text, which no shaper does. The doc comment calls the sets alternatives, but they are applied as a fallback chain. Language systems should come after every script's default LangSys, or be left out.
